name: Differential refraction experiments
summary: Newton's prism experiments showed sunlight is a mixture of colours that bend by different amounts, which explained why simple lens telescopes blur images with colour.
description: Prism investigations leading Newton to identify differing refrangibility among components of sunlight and to diagnose a limitation of simple refracting objectives.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.
why: Newton was working on better telescope lenses and noticed that a prism spread sunlight into an unexpectedly long coloured band.

market.note: Commercial availability is not a milestone of a scientific knowledge result.

date.label: 1666 (reported)
date.basis: Newton's 1672 paper retrospectively dates the initial prism investigations to the beginning of 1666; not contemporaneous publication.

events.statement: Prism investigations leading Newton to identify differing refrangibility among components of sunlight and to diagnose a limitation of simple refracting objectives.
events.caveats: The chronology is Newton's later account. No endorsement of his broader claim that refracting telescopes could never overcome colour error.

evidence.locator: Philosophical Transactions pp. 3075–3079; opening and paragraph beginning When I understood this
evidence.supports: Supplies the retrospective date and states the refrangibility diagnosis.

events.statement: The Royal Society heard Newton’s letter on different refrangibility, thanked him and requested further consideration.
events.caveats: Initial interest and thanks were not settled acceptance; Hooke criticised the theory shortly afterward. The date is Old Style.

evidence.locator: Chapter IV, paragraphs beginning This oddest and most considerable detection and This was communicated
evidence.supports: Reports the 8 February reading, initial thanks and an appointed committee.
